result.title: ActField: Learning Action Effects as Continuous-Time Latent Dynamics
result.summary: Learning how actions change visual states is essential for prediction and decision-making in embodied tasks. Existing action-conditioned JEPA world models typically predict future representations at discrete observation intervals, leaving the temporal evolution of action effects implicit. We introduce ActField, a continuous-time JEPA world model that explicitly models latent state evolution through an action-conditioned vector field integrated over physical time. ActField separates action-independent evolution from action-induced changes, with the latter modulated by the latent context. A reference-conditioned representation and multi-step dynamics loss further support accurate long-horizon prediction. Together, these components provide a structured and temporally continuous formulation for predicting action-conditioned visual dynamics. Experiments across LIBERO, DROID, and BEHAVIOR demonstrate improved visual prediction fidelity and more accurate action-induced motion prediction over existing world models. Further evaluations on simulated and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate the utility of ActField in improving downstream policy planning through VLM-guided action selection.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 ActField，一个连续时间的 JEPA 世界模型：用动作条件化的向量场在物理时间上积分来显式建模 latent 状态演化，并把与动作无关的演化同受 latent 上下文调制的动作引起变化分离开，辅以参考条件表示和多步动力学损失。在 LIBERO、DROID、BEHAVIOR 上报告视觉预测与动作诱发运动预测的提升，并用于 VLM 引导的动作选择与规划。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽属机器人世界模型应用，但其「把状态变化分解为自身演化与条件驱动部分」加多步动力学损失的做法，可供核查 LVR 中推理状态如何逐步更新、如何分配视觉与动作/查询贡献以及长程步数泛化。
